about: Lot 282 (Tappa Prove P0; lab 04/11 on main, Ubuntu 22.04): a host's first container runs, as the agent now reads them. An administrator's non-interactive ssh command runs `sudo podman run` (an image not cached): podman extracts the layers (the kernel's crossing of files created) and opens its bolt_state.db hundreds of times (one file: no crossing any more); at the container's removal podman's CNI plugin flushes its own NAT chain (`iptables -t nat -F CNI-…`). dockerd, at its start, flushes its own isolation chain. Then the same user's rootless podman extracts its own copy of the layers. On main the plugin's flush was NN-L-EVA-002 (`iptables -F`, DefenseImpairment in the administrator's scope) and podman's database the overwrite crossing (ConfirmedIntrusion, root's: privileged), which it corroborated: COMBAT locked, and NEUTRALIZE killed podman. Now: no flush of one user-defined chain is a switch-off, and files created alone are not a mass write — no trigger, no transition, no ladder.
